Cost & prices

How much does NUFI cost? What’s included and what costs extra?

Separate your programme and meal-planning membership from optional physical products.

By Nutrition.Fitness · 15 September 2026 · 4 min read

The short answer

NUFI’s confirmed listed prices are £29.99 per month or £99 paid once for a year. The annual option is equivalent to £8.25 per month; twelve monthly payments total £359.88. NUFI is the programme and meal-planning system, with optional supplements and flavour shots charged separately. The current site is a preview, so working access and final purchase terms must be confirmed before buying.

NUFI’s confirmed listed prices are £29.99 per month or one £99 payment for a year. The annual payment is equivalent to £8.25 per month, but it is paid upfront. Twelve payments of £29.99 total £359.88. Those numbers should be easy to find before you have to enquire.

There is an important availability point: the current Nutrition.Fitness website is a preview. Payment and account access are not connected. The prices have been confirmed for the offer, but a preview screen is not evidence that you can purchase and use every feature today. Final terms and working access need to be clear before you commit.

Monthly and annual costs, plainly

Payment optionPayment amountCost across twelve months
Monthly listed price£29.99 each month£359.88 if twelve payments are made
Annual listed price£99 in one upfront payment£99

The difference across twelve months is £260.88. That does not establish a saving for somebody who would only use a monthly option briefly. Nor does “monthly” confirm cancellation rights or a minimum term: those details must appear in the final membership terms.

There is no confirmed promotional expiry or eligibility condition to add here. If the offers change, the pricing page and purchase information should explain the change rather than leave you to guess.

What is the membership intended to cover?

NUFI is being built as the core system for following a programme and organising meals. The intended experience brings workout programmes, meal planning, progress tracking and AI guidance together. Courses support that experience; the membership is not simply a collection of courses.

Here is the practical distinction: you should be able to understand how a week of training connects with the meals you plan and the progress you record. Before buying, ask to see the working journey for a week like yours. The value depends on that experience, not on how many feature names fit on a page.

Jeff and Steff are the illustrated AI coach characters in the intended experience. Their presence does not mean the membership includes a dedicated human personal trainer, live consultations or individual medical advice. Human coaching hours have not been confirmed in these prices.

What costs extra?

  • Supplements, including any protein products you choose.
  • Flavour shots and other optional physical products.
  • Your ordinary grocery shopping.
  • Any gym access, equipment, travel or individual professional support you choose separately.

Product prices, delivery charges and any product-subscription terms need to be shown with the particular offer. A membership should not leave you discovering compulsory supplement purchases later. Supplements and flavour shots are optional; you can plan meals around ordinary food.

A combined bundle can be convenient, but judge it by its components. Ask for the membership charge, physical products, quantities, delivery frequency and total ongoing payment separately. A bundle should make your decision easier to understand.

Which payment option could suit you?

If the same access is included and you expect to use the service throughout the year, £99 upfront is the lower twelve-month cost. You still need to be comfortable paying that amount at once and satisfied that the working service meets your needs.

If you want a shorter arrangement, ask how the monthly option works in the final terms. Do not assume you can cancel after one payment until that is explicitly confirmed. Equally, do not pay annually because the monthly equivalent looks small if you remain unsure about the service.

Before deciding, list the things you expect to do with NUFI each week. “Choose two suitable sessions and plan the family’s evening meals” is a useful expectation. “Make me a different person” is a lot to ask of an app, particularly before breakfast.

Who should consider something else?

If you want somebody watching your technique in real time, investigate a suitably qualified trainer. If nutrition or exercise is affected by a medical condition, seek appropriate professional guidance. If you already have a routine and only need occasional workout ideas, free resources may be enough.

NUFI needs to earn its place by making the week easier to organise and follow. A person whose needs are already met elsewhere does not need another subscription.

What should be clear before money changes hands?

Confirm the working features included in your option, when access starts, the total payable, any applicable taxes, renewal arrangements, cancellation and refund terms, and the support available. These are normal buying questions, not awkward ones.

Start with the pricing page and explore the programme and recipe approach. Then ask the question that remains unanswered. You should understand both the price and what you are choosing before making the decision.

Sources and checks

Information checked on 15 September 2026. Prices, availability and subscriptions can change; check the linked provider before paying.
